title: Evaluation for finite locally free module sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module: there is an open cover $(V_a)$ of $X$ such that $\mathcal F|_{V_a}\cong\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus d_a}$ for integers $d_a\geq0$ (compare the constant-rank notion of [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]). For every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$, the canonical evaluation morphism $\mathcal F^{\vee}\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$, where $\mathcal F^{\vee}:=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal O_X)$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, natural in $\mathcal G$. Here tensor product, sheaf Hom, its group of global sections, and sheaves of modules use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pur-sheaf-hom], [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module], and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: The existing proved source-library instance AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isIso_dualTensorHom_of_isFiniteLocallyFree, in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.HomTensor.LocallyFree, establishes IsIso (dualTensorHom F G) for every coefficient module G, with precisely the variable-local-rank IsFiniteLocallyFree hypothesis of this statement. It already implements the finite-free local calculation and locally bijective sheafification argument of the original plan. Take e G = CategoryTheory.asIso (dualTensorHom F G). Its hom is definitionally dualTensorHom F G, proving the first required equality.

The proved source-library lemma AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.dualTensorHom_naturality_right F g states (dual F ◁ g) ≫ dualTensorHom F H = dualTensorHom F G ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (𝟙 F) g. Since (e G).hom is definitionally dualTensorHom F G, its symmetry proves the required naturality equality.

lean.statement: theorem dual_tensor_hom_iso (X : Scheme.{u}) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteLocallyFree] : ∃ e : (∀ G : X.Modules, Scheme.Modules.tensorObj (dual F) G ≅ homObj F G), (∀ G : X.Modules, (e G).hom = dualTensorHom F G) ∧ ∀ {G H : X.Modules} (g : G ⟶ H), (e G).hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := X.sheaf) (𝟙 F) g = (dual F ◁ g) ≫ (e H).hom
